Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The center of the hurricane narrowly missed the North Carolina Outer Banks, where winds of 72 mph were recorded in Hatteras. Small craft and light-framed buildings suffered damage but impacts were otherwise negligible.

In Baltimore, rushing water up to 5 ft (1.5 m) stalled vehicles and displaced some nearly a block away. Two buildings were electrically charged for unknown reasons during the storm, shocking one person before the structures were roped off.
In Hempstead Harbor, an inn was washed from its piles and demolished.
At the Suffolk County Fairgrounds, an automobile building saw a large section of its sheet metal roof torn off.
In Patchogue, a garage was flattened and several small signs were torn loose and damaged.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: In Queens, four buildings, including a school, were struck by lightning; one home was partially destroyed.
In Fair Haven, New Jersey, a 69-year-old man was killed after being electrocuted by a live wire downed by the storm.
Along the coastline, the United States Coast Guard attempted search and rescue of the SS Morro Castle which caught fire and killed 137 people on board.
Three crewmen of the schooner Neshaminy died when it capsized off Brigantine.
In New York, two seaman drowned when their tugboat overturned in New York Bay.
Further still, a man died after his sailboat overturned in rough seas near Northport, Long Island.
In the eastern section of the borough, a man died after crashing his vehicle in the downpours in Queens.
On Lake Ontario, a Canadian National Railway car ferry was unexpectedly hit by a large wave, severely damaging the ship and injuring 52 people.
In Peconic Bay specifically, damage to nearly 50 boats amounted to $10,000. Docks likewise suffered substantial damage.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Over 10,000 people were killed in India when Tropical Cyclone 03A brought a 4.9-metre (16-foot) storm surge to the Kathiawar Peninsula, inundating numerous salt mines.
Tropical Cyclone 01B killed at least 26 people and left at least 4,000 fishermen missing in eastern Bangladesh on May 20.
A short lived depression in mid-October killed 122 people after triggering severe flooding in Andhra Pradesh.
In November, Tropical Cyclone 06B killed six people and caused property damage worth BTN 880 million (US$20.7 million) in eastern India.
An additional 40 people were killed and 100 fishermen were listed as missing after Tropical Cyclone 07B affected Bangladesh.
Total damages from the storm amounted to Rs. 120 billion (US$3 billion).
In November, Tropical Cyclone 06B killed six people and caused property damage worth BTN 880 million (US$20.7 million) in eastern India.

Hazards_Annotation: The text mentions that Tropical Cyclone 03A brought a 4.9-metre storm surge that inundated salt mines, and a short lived depression triggered severe flooding in Andhra Pradesh, which clearly indicates flood hazards.

In June, the second cyclone of the season may have also caused fatalities in Cuba.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: At about 5:00 am, a 30-foot section of floodwall on the east side of the Industrial Canal breached and released flood water into the adjacent Lower Ninth Ward, a dense lower to middle class neighborhood of primarily Black homeowners.

By 6:30 a.m. CDT, levees along the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, lining the south side of New Orleans East, overtopped and breached, and the surge flooded the primarily middle to upper class Black region.

Between 6 and 7:00 am on the west edge of New Orleans, a monolith on the east side of the London Avenue Canal failed and allowed water over 10 feet deep into Fillmore Gardens, a mostly Black middle class neighborhood.
At about 6:30 a.m., several monoliths failed on the 17th Street Canal and a torrent of water blasted into Lakeview, a mainly white middle class neighborhood of homeowners.

At approximately 7:45 a.m. CDT, a much larger second hole opened up in the Industrial Canal, and floodwaters from the two breaches combined to submerge the entire historic Lower Ninth Ward in over 10 feet of water.

Between 7 and 8:00 am, the west side of the London Avenue Canal breached, in addition to the east side, and flooded the adjacent mixed-race neighborhood of homeowners (specific neighborhood name not provided).

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Extensive damage was caused in central Lismore from large hail and strong winds. Many buildings were damaged including City Hall, the police station, ambulance station, hospital and other council buildings and small businesses. City Hall had massive damage on its western side and partly collapsed; the Gymnastics Centre roof also partly collapsed due to the weight of hail and water. Damage bill was estimated at $60 million with Lismore declared a natural disaster area.

Three weeks later, another storm caused chaos in the small town of Dunoon. More than 20 houses lost their roofs—with some partly demolished, including the local church—as tornadic winds swept through the centre. Trees were snapped or uprooted, power lines brought down, and gardens flattened. Large hail was reported and the local sub-station exploded after being hit by flying debris, leading to power outages. The Lismore district was declared a natural disaster area for the second time with the damage bill at Dunoon estimated at $5 million.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Tropical Cyclone Sigma caused destruction from Townsville to Brisbane between 24 and 27 January 1896. 18 people were killed, most of whom lost their lives when a storm surge caused a breach of the Ross River on 26 January, flooding parts of Townsville.[44][45]

Cyclone Mahina, in March 1899, resulted in the greatest death toll of any natural disaster in Australian history. Over 400 people lost their lives. The storm decimated a pearling fleet at Bathurst Bay in Queensland and deaths included the crews of around 100 vessels and an estimated 100 local aboriginals, who were swept out to sea while trying to save shipwrecked crew.[46]
The Mackay Cyclone struck Mackay and surrounding regions in late January 1918, experiencing the death of some 30 people.[48]
10 March 1918 saw an even stronger cyclone cross the coast at Innisfail, with 37 people perishing in the township of Innisfail.[49]
10 March 1918 saw an even stronger cyclone with a further 40-60 Aboriginals estimated to have died in outlying areas.[49]
A cyclone in Northern Queensland killed 99 people over two days in mid March 1934.[50]
A cyclone struck the Gold Coast on 20 February 1954. Four people were killed during the cyclone.[51]
A cyclone struck the Gold Coast on 20 February 1954, and a further 22 died in the resulting floods around Lismore in Northern New South Wales.[52]
